about: tools/workflows/recipes: rebuilt on the notice tables (devices, notices). Replaces tool:act-on-my-notice in tools/tell-the-person. A notice offers one action, open, to its url; an action that posts to another app, or needs its source to run first, is refused with the owner that must act.

payload.label: Act on one of my notices
payload.job: Carry out the action a notice offers in the person's own database: an open of a path on this site (the notice is marked read and the path is returned to open), or a refusal that says which owner must act.
payload.produces: The path to open and the notice read, or the reason the action was not performed.

source.from: tools/tell-the-person read-data/told.mjs (actOnMyNotice) and tool:act-on-my-notice, read on the Workshop's origin/main 75fa3807fc, then rebuilt on notices.url
source.note: The refusals are kept word for word. The mark is the same write as workflow:mark-my-notices-read: it only writes a notice whose read_at is still null, so a repeated press writes nothing new except acted_at.

database.description: The name of the person's own database, the one the workflow's tables live in (the store the account keeps its rows in).

action.description: The id of the action the notice offered: open (its url) or reply (text typed on the device)

text.description: The words of a reply; required for reply, kept on the notice as answer_text

submission_id.description: The device's id for one reply; a retry of the same words is answered done and written once

steps.title: Make the notice tables if they are absent
steps.do: Run the statements of this step's sql, in order, through tool:run-sql-in-my-database with database = input.database. They only create or add what is missing, so a run where the tables and columns exist changes nothing. Submit {rendered: true}.

sql.name: devices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (id text PRIMARY KEY, platform text NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('live', 'web-push', 'apns')), token text, app_build text, registered_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())

sql.name: notices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notices (id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, device_id text REFERENCES devices (id), title text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', url text, made_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), read_at timestamptz, acted_at timestamptz)

sql.name: answers
sql.text: ALTER TABLE notices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS answer_text text, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS answered_at timestamptz

steps.title: Carry out the offered action, or refuse it
steps.do: Check the input: id must be "told:<number>" and action must be non-empty text; otherwise refuse with "Name the notice id and one offered action id.". Make the notice number: the number after "told:". Run the statement named notice with params [notice number]. When it returns no row, refuse with "There is no such notice.". When action is "reply": trim text; when the trimmed text is empty, refuse with "Write the reply to send."; when answered_at is set and answer_text equals the trimmed text, answer {done: true, said: "Reply kept."} and write nothing (a retry of the same reply); when answered_at is set with other words, refuse with "This notice was already answered."; otherwise run the statement named reply with params [notice number, trimmed text] and answer {done: true, said: "Reply kept."}. When action is not "open" or "reply", refuse with "That action was not offered by this notice.". When action is "open" and the notice's url is null, refuse with "That action was not offered by this notice.". When action is "open" and url is not a path on this site (it must begin with a single / and hold no backslash), refuse with "This action needs its source owner to act; it was not performed.". Otherwise run the statement named act with the same params: it marks the notice read and sets acted_at. Answer {done: true, said: "Opening the notice.", open: url}. A refused action writes nothing.

sql.name: notice
sql.text: SELECT id, url, answer_text, answered_at FROM notices WHERE id = $1::bigint

sql.name: act
sql.text: UPDATE notices SET read_at = coalesce(read_at, now()), acted_at = now() WHERE id = $1::bigint

sql.name: reply
sql.text: UPDATE notices SET answer_text = $2, answered_at = now(), read_at = coalesce(read_at, now()), acted_at = now() WHERE id = $1::bigint AND answered_at IS NULL
